propositions: DC transport raises jira.exceptions.JIRAError which is not caught by existing urllib.error.HTTPError handlers in dispatch_apply_phases.py and outbound_differ.py, causing exceptions to escape and fail soft-degradation logic
deletion detection in outbound_differ._safe_get_issue silently breaks on DC because JIRAError does not match the HTTPError.code==404 condition or URLError/TimeoutError/OSError handlers
core reconciler modules depend on transport-specific exception types (urllib.error.HTTPError) creating a vendor leak that does not scale to multiple backends
BackendHTTPError must be declared as a port contract, subclass urllib.error.HTTPError to preserve .code access, and be raised by all backends at their adapter boundary
DC transport must translate JIRAError to BackendHTTPError at _with_connection_retry, the single choke point for all DC methods, preserving the HTTP status code
existing catch clauses in core modules must remain unchanged; subclass relationship ensures they match BackendHTTPError and classification logic (404→_DELETED, 4xx→soft-degrade) works without edits
